decisions.evidence: R1 maker draft spec: user must 'type in the title myself' and app 'won't look anything up'. R1 client point 1: 'When I paste a web address, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title (and ideally a short description and the little site icon) and fill those in for me, so I can just tweak them if needed.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Draft contradicts REF-BM-02 (auto-collect metadata) and REF-BM-03 (edit collected fields). Client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (auto-fill + editable), so catch_type=correct. Save-by-url (REF-BM-01) itself conformed.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: draft search is 'plain word matching' (client's paraphrase confirmed by maker's later 'smarter search' additions). R1 client point 2: 'search my tags directly (something like typing #recipes)', 'combine terms — like this AND that, one OR the other, this but NOT that, and putting quotes around a phrase to match it exactly.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Draft omits #tag (REF-BM-14), boolean/grouping operators (REF-BM-15), and quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16). Client supplies each expected behaviour → correct. R2 maker added #tag/AND/OR/NOT/quoted/parenthesized search.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker draft covers 'tagging' but no autocomplete. R1 client point 3: 'When I'm adding a tag to a bookmark, I'd want it to suggest tags I've already used so I don't accidentally make three slightly different versions of the same tag.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Existing-tag autocomplete (REF-BM-10) is a related reference requirement missing from the presented tagging scope; client requests it → extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker draft covers 'favoriting' and 'filtering', not read-later. R1 client point 4: 'the thing I really care about is marking a link as something I still need to read, and then being able to look at just those unread ones on their own... Favoriting my best links and tracking what I haven't gotten to yet feel like two different needs.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Presented scope substitutes favorites (an extra, non-reference feature) and lacks read-later/unread. Client identifies the difference and requests the missing reference requirement (mark unread REF-BM-17, dedicated unread view REF-BM-18, mark read REF-BM-19) → extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker exclusion list: 'imports... are outside the initial scope.' R1 client: 'Everything else — accounts, sharing, syncing, folders, imports, and browser add-ons being left out for now — I'm okay with for a first version.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Netscape-HTML import (REF-BM-30) is a reference extended item excluded by the maker. Client explicitly names 'imports' and accepts the departure for v1 without requesting alignment → accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. (Export REF-BM-31 was neither presented nor named, so not counted here.) Sharing/sync/folders are not reference items; accounts/browser-extensions are infra (REF-BM-I01/I04) excluded from the denominator.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: 'Explicit marking as read; merely opening a link does not mark it read.' R2 client: 'opening a link doesn't mark it read on its own, only when I say so. That's the behavior I'd want, so please keep it.'
decisions.note: Spec review. Conforms to reference — REF-BM-19 makes marking-as-read an explicit action and REF-BM-08 defines opening as navigation only; the reference never requires auto-mark-on-open. Recorded conforming decision, not an opportunity.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: 'automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval'; R5 maker: 'automatic title, description, and favicon retrieval'. R2 client praises 'the title, description, and icon filled in'; R5 client: 'it pulled in the title, description, and icon on its own' — preview image never mentioned by client at any round.
decisions.note: Spec gate / implementation review. REF-BM-02 requires title, description, favicon AND preview image; the presented metadata scope consistently lists only three fields, omitting the preview image. The core auto-collection divergence was caught at R1, but this remaining preview-image aspect of REF-BM-02 passed each subsequent presentation without a corrective response or explicit expression → unexpressed_divergence.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker MVP: 'prevent duplicates'. R5 client: 'Trying to save the same link again stopped me and pointed me back to the one I already had.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Duplicate-url handling converging to editing the existing bookmark conforms to REF-BM-06. Recorded conforming decision, confirmed working; not an opportunity.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker delivers app with editing and 'confirmation-protected deletion' but no archive. R5 client: 'being able to tuck links away in an archive rather than only deleting them... but those are new ideas for a later round, not anything wrong with what you've delivered. Please just note them for next time.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Delivered app lacks archiving (REF-BM-26 hide-but-keep) distinct from deletion (REF-BM-27 archive reversible vs delete permanent). Client explicitly states the expected behaviour and its difference from delete, then accepts the departure for this version → accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. (REF-BM-28 archived-list view not explicitly named.)

decisions.evidence: R5 maker delivers search but no saved filters. R5 client: 'saving a favorite search so I can jump back to it — but those are new ideas for a later round, not anything wrong with what you've delivered. Please just note them for next time.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Delivered app lacks saving a search term + tag combination as a reusable bundle (REF-BM-29). Client explicitly expresses the expectation and accepts its absence for v1 → accepted_divergence, catch_type=none.
